name: go-fly
shape: Go RSS reader on Fly.io: one binary serves the API and the embedded web UI, refreshes feeds on an hourly ticker, keeps everything in SQLite on a Fly volume

platform.name: Fly.io
platform.why: fly.toml with [http_service], auto_stop_machines and a [[mounts]] volume at /data

processes.note: cmd/main.go builds the one binary; the UI under internal/web/public is embedded and served by it; min_machines_running = 1 keeps one machine on

data.note: DB_PATH /data/agg.db on the lite_reader_data volume; opened with modernc.org/sqlite in internal/app.go

breaks.note: time.NewTicker every hour in a goroutine started from internal/app.go fetches all feeds; with CPU only during requests it stalls, with several instances it runs on each
sql.Open("sqlite", dsn) on a file on the Fly volume; Cloud Run has no volume that a SQLite writer can share

notBreaks.why: browser code served as a static asset; setTimeout in the drag and drop handler
vendored Go modules (go build -mod=vendor): third-party code, never a finding of this app
os.Create(dbPath) creates the database file the SQLite finding already moves; one change, not two

notes: The web UI is Preact loaded from internal/web/public and embedded into the binary, so it is served by the Go process but runs in the browser. Sessions are rows in SQLite (internal/app/auth), not memory. Goose migrations run at start-up from embedded SQL, not in a release step. docker-compose.yaml is the self-hosting variant with the same binary and a ./data bind mount.
